reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered audit, in a multi-step ALFWorld agent with a Qwen3-32B reader, of whether the counterfactual value of a retrieved memory item is additive: pairwise removal interaction I(a,b) is measured on three manufactured item classes (planted conflicting, complementary fragments, cross-type control) and, on the retriever's own top-3 sets, LOO and exact Shapley credit are computed on disjoint seed halves to ask whether the two estimators disagree with each other more than each disagrees with itself; a content-held-fixed copy-count arm and a split-half reliability-versus-seed-count curve turn estimator noise and re-run cost into reported estimands.
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv:2605.05716, 'More Is Not Always Better: Cross-Component Interference in LLM Agent Scaffolding' (2026-05-07; VERIFIED via the literature command, returned by both S2 and HF). It already runs an exact-Shapley factorial inside an LLM agent and reports destructive interference with 56% submodularity violations — i.e. 'removal is not additive in a multi-step agent' is an existing, published finding; only the unit changes (retrieved bank items rather than scaffold components). The proposal names it but dismisses it in one clause, which understates the threat: a reviewer will ask why the same non-additivity, already demonstrated one level up in the same kind of system, is a new claim one level down. Two further verified co-threats: CUE-R arXiv:2604.05467 (VERIFIED via `paper`, 2026-04-07, cit 2) already does intervention-based per-evidence-item utility with a REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE taxonomy and reports non-additive multi-hop interactions, which pre-empts both the intervention design and the dose arm modulo the single-shot/multi-step gap; and arXiv:2507.04480 'Source Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation' (VERIFIED via `paper`, PKDD/ECML Workshops 2025, cit 7) already compares approximate against exact Shapley document attribution under redundancy/complementarity/synergy while explicitly minimising costly LLM interactions, which is the cost-versus-fidelity half of P1/P6 in the document setting. What is genuinely unclaimed after my searches: the prevalence of interaction on a retriever's own natural sets, and the seed-count/LLM-call price of a stable per-item rank in an agent. That residue is real but thin for a main-track claim.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline is confounded with the bounded binary outcome, and the proposal never says the word. Success rates here are 0.54 (k=0) to 0.81/0.87 (k=3), so removals from the natural top-3 set operate against a ceiling. Additivity of removal effects is scale-dependent: a data-generating process that is exactly additive in log-odds produces non-zero I on the probability scale, and — because LOO uses only the top face of the lattice while Shapley averages marginals across coalition sizes 0-2 where the compression differs — produces systematic LOO-vs-Shapley rank disagreement with literally zero interaction. Every headline number (P1's 0.15 correlation gap, the >=20% top-item flips, P2's I <= -8, P3's I >= +8) is therefore consistent with 'no interaction, just a squashed scale', and the pre-registered refuters do not distinguish the two. A second, compounding problem: P1 asks for a 0.15 difference between two split-half Spearman correlations whose absolute size the proposal itself predicts is low — P6 predicts LOO split-half reliability <= 0.5 at 2 seeds per half and >= 0.7 only at 4, and P1's halves are 3 seeds each, so both correlations being compared sit in the attenuated 0.4-0.6 range where a 0.15 gap is a large fraction of the measurable range and is not robust to which cells happen to be noisy. P1 and P6 are the same measured quantity pulling in opposite directions: the seed-cost result, if it confirms, undermines the precision the headline needs. Third, the proposal asserts 'the less noisy Shapley can only agree better' without arithmetic. It happens to be defensible — the Shapley weight vector over the eight cells has sum of squared weights 5/9 against LOO's 2, so exact Shapley is roughly 3.5x lower-variance per item at matched seeds — but that is exactly why the comparison is unfair in the other direction: Shapley consumes 8 runs per set to LOO's 4, so the headline compares an estimator at 2x the compute. Fourth, per-item rank correlations pooled over 600 items nested in 200 games will be dominated by between-game variance in how much any item helps (easy games where every removal does nothing, hard games where none does); the within-set top-item statistic is the honest one and is demoted to secondary. Fifth, the automated entailment flags are largely right on their own terms: P6's falsifier (2 seeds per half reaching 0.7) is unreachable given the noise floor the program has already measured, and P7's confirm band (|I' - I| <= 3) is half its own propagated CI, so P7 can never confirm and its 3-to-12 dead zone is where noise lands.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register the additivity test on a scale that is not mechanically non-additive: report I on the logit scale alongside the probability scale, and add an outcome with headroom (steps-to-goal, subgoal/procedure-step completion) as a co-primary, so 'removal is not additive' cannot be satisfied by ceiling compression alone. (2) Score P1 against a generative null rather than against rho_LOO: simulate the eight-cell lattice from the measured base rates under exact additivity-in-log-odds with the measured per-cell binomial noise, push it through both estimators, and report the expected cross-versus-within gap and top-item flip rate that this zero-interaction world produces; the claim is then the excess over that null, not over a hand-argued inequality. (3) State the variance arithmetic that licenses the 'Shapley can only agree better' step (weight sum-of-squares 5/9 versus 2) and score against the attenuation ceiling sqrt(rho_LOO * rho_SH) using the Shapley-vs-Shapley floor already being collected. (4) Match the estimators on LLM calls, not seeds: 8-run LOO (6 seeds) versus 8-run exact Shapley (3 seeds); this is the comparison the 'which estimator to trust, at what cost' conclusion actually needs. (5) Compute the rank agreement within set (3 items) as primary, with the pooled correlation as secondary. (6) Pair BACKGROUND with CONFLICT on the same (game, seed) and add seeds until the propagated half-width is <= 3 so P7 can confirm; move P6's falsifier to a value the measured floor permits (e.g. falsify at >= 0.35 at 2 seeds per half). (7) Add one decision arm so the audit has a consequence: prune or re-rank the bank by LOO credit versus by Shapley credit versus at random, and re-measure end-task success — without it the paper's conclusion is 'our estimator is noisy', which the brief already suspected.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. First and decisive: a budget-matched LOO. The plan compares LOO on 3 seeds (4 runs/set) against exact Shapley on 3 seeds (8 runs/set) and then draws a conclusion about which estimator to trust; a reviewer will demand LOO at 8 runs per set (double the seeds) against Shapley at 8 runs per set, since that is the choice a practitioner actually faces and it is the one comparison that can make Shapley lose. The cost-per-unit-reliability table gestures at this but the headline estimand does not use it. Second: a downstream decision baseline — select/prune bank items by LOO credit, by Shapley credit, by the DIG-style confidence proxy, and at random, then re-measure task success — so that 'per-item credit is estimator-dependent' is shown to cost something. Minor third: a permuted-credit placebo (shuffle item labels within game) to give the floor of the split-half rank agreement, which the no-op repeat does not provide at the item level.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is well above the norm for this program: five queries with IDs, one home-vocabulary query with no agent/memory words, and one id verified with `paper`. My searches (all via the literature command; S2 and HF both answered every query; WebSearch unavailable this session, WebFetch not used): Q-A 'non-additive interaction between co-retrieved memory items pairwise removal agent' --recent -> 10 hits, closest arXiv:2607.10608 (compliance trap) and arXiv:2604.05467 (CUE-R); nothing measuring pairwise removal interaction in a multi-step agent. Q-B 'leave-one-out versus Shapley value disagreement ranking data valuation noisy evaluation' -> arXiv:2205.15466 Data Banzhaf (AISTATS, cit 196), arXiv:2410.01649 shapiq, arXiv:2107.11357 joint Shapley, arXiv:2602.01399 OddSHAP, arXiv:2406.04606 FreeShap. Q-C 'Shapley context attribution memory entries agentic learner multimodal' --recent -> EMPTY (reported as empty, not as novelty); DG-Mem instead verified by id. Q-D 'Shapley value in-context demonstration selection interaction non-additivity example set' -> only generic SHAP/interaction-index tooling (2410.01649, 2107.11357, 2404.01332, 1705.07874); no ICL/demonstration-set interaction paper surfaced. Q-E 'duplicate copies of the same document in context repetition effect RAG' --recent -> arXiv:2605.27105 (position and context-size effects in RAG), arXiv:2603.12396 (de-duplication at test time); nothing holding content fixed while varying copy count. Q-F 'cross-component interference agent scaffolding factorial submodularity violation' --recent -> arXiv:2605.05716 VERIFIED. Q-G 'per-item memory utility estimate variance number of rollouts needed reliable ranking' --recent -> arXiv:2602.07150 'On Randomness in Agentic Evals' (run-to-run variance of agentic evaluation, relevant and uncited) and rollout-budget allocation work (2607.22002, 2606.11119); nothing on per-item credit reliability. IDs I verified: 2604.05467, 2507.04480, 2608.23268 (all via `paper`), 2605.05716, 2607.10608, 2410.01649, 2107.11357, 2602.17107, 2602.01399 (all returned by search). IDs the proposal relies on that I could NOT verify in this session: 2608.02508 (RoMeRL), 2605.08374 (MemQ), 2509.12765 (DIG), 2511.10687, 2506.23799 (KAIROS), 2605.01284, 2601.03786 — none of them load-bearing for the novelty argument, but the Related Work leans on RoMeRL and MemQ unverified. The one real failure of the proposal's check is Q5: it reports 'no results' for LOO-versus-Shapley agreement under stochastic evaluation and concludes the space is empty, but the correct home vocabulary is semivalue/Banzhaf under a noisy utility function, and Data Banzhaf (arXiv:2205.15466, verified) is precisely a study of which value estimator ranks reliably when the utility evaluation is stochastic, with a rank-stability 'safety margin' as its central object. That is not a collision — different domain (training-data valuation, not co-retrieved context in an agent) — but it is a required citation, it supplies the estimator this proposal should have included as a third arm, and it means the estimator-noise contribution is less unexplored than the check claims.
